title: Questionnaire answer starter kit & log-mapping for SIEM exports
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight starter kit for responding to customer security questionnaires (SOC/enterprise vendors/RFPs) that hit three hard topics: RBAC v2, audit log schema, and SIEM export/evidence automation. The doc bundles short, copy-pasteable answer patterns, pointers to canonical evidence, and notes for the Trust Center one-pager. Meant for Solutions and Security SMEs to accelerate responses and ensure consistency.

Status/usage guidance:
- Draft — use as a living scratchpad.
- When copying answers into a questionnaire: keep the short description + provide links to the canonical artifact (Confluence/Jira/GitHub) and attach the specific exported evidence if requested.
- For legal-sensitive customers: loop in Security Ops and Privacy for sign-off (see linked artifacts).

TL;DR one-paragraph summary for customer-facing one-pager (copyable):
Redwood Inference provides role-based access control (RBAC v2) with fine-grained role and permission groups, immutable audit logging for authentication and data-plane actions, and configurable SIEM exports (syslog/S3/agent) for ingestion into customer SIEMs. We support evidence exports for attestations (time-bounded snapshots), and our automation tooling can produce on-demand trace bundles that map directly to common questionnaire fields. Contact security-questions@redwood.com for tailored packages and audit access.

Core answer patterns (short + expanded):
1) RBAC v2 (short)
- Short: "Redwood implements RBAC v2: role templates + resource scoping with least-privilege defaults. Admins can create custom roles, assign to principals, and inherit via org/team groups. Role changes are versioned and recorded in audit logs."
- Expanded (when asked for specifics): "RBAC v2 supports: role templates (admin, developer, billing, audit-reader), resource scoping (model, project, environment), attribute-based constraints (time-bound grants, IP allow-lists), and grants export. Role change events emit audit records with actor_id, actor_type, role_id, effected_resource, change_type, request_id, timestamp. See Audit Log Schema doc (linked)."
- Evidence to attach: RBAC schema diagram (Confluence), sample role JSON export, screenshot of Console role editor, audit-snapshot for a role change (zip).

2) Audit log schema (short)
- Short: "All control-plane and user-triggered data-plane events are logged with a standardized schema: event_type, actor_id, actor_type, resource, action, outcome, timestamp, request_id, correlation_id. Logs are immutable and retained per contract."
- Expanded (when asked for fields): "Primary fields we populate:
  - event_type (control|data|system)
  - event_subtype (e.g., auth.login, model.infer, role.update)
  - actor_id, actor_type (user, service, system)
  - resource_type, resource_id (project/model/deployment)
  - action (create/read/update/delete/execute)
  - outcome (success|failure|partial)
  - request_id, correlation_id, trace_id
  - timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - metadata map (free-form JSON key/value, includes request parameters like prompt_id, token_count)
Notes: we avoid logging raw prompt text by default for hosted customers unless contractually required; for private deployments the customer controls data plane logging policy.
- Evidence to attach: audit-log-schema.pdf, sample-logs-2025-10-01.jsonl (redacted), retention policy excerpt."

3) SIEM export and evidence automation (short)
- Short: "We support push and pull export modes for audit logs and telemetry: syslog (TLS), S3 export (parquet/json), and direct connector to customers' SIEM via secure agent. Exports include the canonical schema and mapping file. Evidence automation can produce a time-bound exported bundle and an integrity hash."
- Expanded: "Export options:
  - Real-time syslog over TLS (recommended for SIEMs that ingest syslog).
  - S3-delivered batches (hourly/daily) in JSONL or parquet.
  - HTTPS webhook/pull endpoints with signed URLs for short-term access.
  - Optional Kafka/Streaming connectors for high-throughput customers.
Automation pipeline: an evidence automation job can: 1) accept a request (ticket id or questionnaire id), 2) run a query against the log-store for the requested time range and event types, 3) redact configurable fields (PII/prompt content), 4) store the result bundle in a secure S3 with object lock, 5) produce a SHA256 manifest and signed delivery link."
- Evidence to attach: sample-siem-mapping.csv, automation-job-runbook.md, example-delivery-manifest.txt.

FAQ / common questionnaire Qs + suggested answers (copyable)
Q: "Can we get a per-user access list for Model X for the last 90 days?"
A: "Yes — we can provide a time-bounded audit bundle that includes role grants and model.infer events filtered by resource_id. Typically provided as a redacted JSONL export with actor_id pseudonymization if requested. File format: JSONL; delivery: secure S3 link; retention: per contract."

Q: "Do you log request/response payloads?"
A: "By default, we log metadata and token counts; payloads (prompt/response) are not persisted in audit logs for hosted customers unless explicitly enabled via contract. For Private deployments the customer can configure data-plane persistence. See Privacy policy in Trust Center."

Q: "How do you ensure log integrity?"
A: "Logs are written to an append-only store with immutability settings. Export bundles include a SHA256 manifest and may be stored behind object lock/SSE-KMS as required. We also provide signed attestations from the automation pipeline. See automation runbook."

Mapping guidance for Solutions Engineers (how to find canonical artifacts quickly)
- RBAC evidence: Confluence > RBAC v2 Spec (linked), GitHub > role-schema/export endpoint (PR 2567), Console screenshots folder: /evidence/rbac/screenshots/
- Audit logs: S3 path: s3://redwood-logs/audit-schema/samples/; sample exports under /evidence/audit-samples/
- SIEM mapping: /evidence/siem/mappings/ with a CSV mapping file for Splunk/QRadar/Elastic.

Checklist when preparing a customer bundle:
1) Confirm scope (time range, resources, redaction requirements)
2) Pull RBAC exports and role-change events for scope window
3) Pull infer/auth logs with request_id correlation for the same window
4) Run automation job with redaction rules and object-lock storage
5) Generate manifest (SHA256), include script that produced the bundle, and collect signatures
6) Attach mapping docs and a short readme (one-page) describing fields
7) Share via secure link and log the delivery in the ticketing system (SEC-842 pattern)

Trust Center one-pager draft copy (customer-facing)
Title: "How Redwood answers security questionnaires quickly"
Blurb: "We provide standardized controls and evidence packages for RBAC, audit logs, and SIEM integrations so you can accelerate your security reviews. Our evidence automation generates tamper-evident bundles with redaction and delivery options suited to enterprise needs."
Bullets:
- RBAC v2: fine-grained roles, scoped grants, versioned role-change logs
- Audit logs: standardized schema, immutable storage, configurable retention
- SIEM exports: syslog/S3/webhook connectors and mapping templates for common SIEMs
- Evidence automation: on-demand bundles, signed manifests, and delivery tracking
Call to action: "Request an evidence package: security-questions@redwood.com or open SEC-842 for a guided delivery."

Open items / TODOs (action owners in parens)
- Add redaction templates for prompt content (Research/Privacy)
- Produce Splunk and Elastic native mapping files (Observability)
- Create a Customer-ready one-pager PDF and place in Trust Center (Marketing + Security Ops)
- Add a small script to the automation pipeline to include human-readable CSV summaries for auditors (Platform Eng)

Appendix: quick snippets to paste into questionnaires
- "Describe your RBAC model": paste the RBAC short answer + link to RBAC v2 spec + attached role-export.json
- "Provide sample audit records": attach sample-logs-2025-10-01.jsonl (redacted) and include the mapping CSV
- "How logs are exported to our SIEM": paste the SIEM short answer and include mapping file and recommended ingestion settings (syslog+TLS recommended).
